# base62 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/base62/

## Expand description

`base62` is a `no_std` crate that provides base62 encoding and decoding functionality.

With the `alloc` feature (enabled by default), it provides functions for converting
between `u128` values and base62 strings using both standard (0-9, A-Z, a-z) and
alternative (0-9, a-z, A-Z) alphabets.

When used without default features, it provides the core encoding and decoding primitives that operate on byte slices.

For usage with the standard library’s IO traits, enable the `std` feature.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Decode](https://docs.rs/enum.DecodeError.html)- Error
- Indicates the cause of a decoding failure in base62 decoding operations.
- [Encode](https://docs.rs/enum.EncodeError.html)- Error
- Indicates the cause of an encoding failure in encoding operations.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [decode](https://docs.rs/fn.decode.html)
- Decodes a base62 byte slice or an equivalent, like a `String`, using the standard digit ordering (0 to 9, then A to Z, then a to z).
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_alternative.html)- alternative
- Decodes a base62 byte slice or an equivalent, like a `String`, using the alternative digit ordering (0 to 9, then a to z, then A to Z) with lowercase letters before uppercase letters.
- [encode](https://docs.rs/fn.encode.html)
- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the standard digit ordering
(0 to 9, then A to Z, then a to z), and returns the resulting
`String`
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_alternative.html)- alternative
- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the alternative digit ordering
(0 to 9, then a to z, then A to Z) with lowercase letters before uppercase letters,
and returns the resulting `String`
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_alternative_buf.html)- alternative_ - buf
- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the alternative digit ordering
(0 to 9, then a to z, then A to Z) with lowercase letters before uppercase letters, and
then appends it onto the end of the given `String`
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_alternative_bytes.html)- alternative_ - bytes
- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the alternative digit ordering (0 to 9, then a to z, then A to Z), and writes it to the passed buffer.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_buf.html)- buf
- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the standard digit ordering
(0 to 9, then A to Z, then a to z), and then appends it onto the end of the given
`String`
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_bytes.html)- bytes
- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the standard digit ordering (0 to 9, then A to Z, then a to z), and writes it to the passed buffer.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_fmt.html)- fmt
- Writes the base62 representation of a number using the standard alphabet to any fmt::Write destination.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_fmt_alt.html)- fmt_ - alt
- Writes the base62 representation of a number using the alternative alphabet to any fmt::Write destination.

---

# base62 2.2.4 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/base62/latest

# base62

A fast, zero-dependency base62 encoder/decoder library for Rust, typically used in URL shorteners. It supports both standard [0-9A-Za-z] and alternative [0-9a-zA-Z] variants.

## Features

- `no_std`compatible with optional- `alloc`and- `std`support
- Encodes integers up to `u128`
- Zero-copy decoding
- Efficient string handling
- Two encoding variants:
- Standard [0-9A-Za-z]
- Alternative [0-9a-zA-Z]

## Usage

Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "2"
```
### Basic Example

```
use base62;
// Encoding
let encoded = encode;
assert_eq!;
// Decoding
let decoded = decode.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
```
### No-std Usage

The crate works in `no_std` environments by default:

```
use base62;
// Encode into a fixed buffer
let mut buf = ;  // Maximum size needed for u128
let len = encode_bytes.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
// Decode from bytes
let decoded = decode.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
```
## Feature Flags

- `alloc`: Enables String allocation support (enabled by default)
- `std`: Enables std::io traits support

## Performance

The library is optimized for both encoding and decoding performance:

- Zero-copy decoding
- Efficient buffer management
- Direct string manipulation for optimal performance when appending

## License

Licensed under the MIT license. See LICENSE for details.

# criterion - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/criterion/^0.7/

## Expand description

A statistics-driven micro-benchmarking library written in Rust.

This crate is a microbenchmarking library which aims to provide strong statistical confidence in detecting and estimating the size of performance improvements and regressions, while also being easy to use.

See
[the user guide](https://bheisler.github.io/criterion.rs/book/index.html)
for examples as well as details on the measurement and analysis process,
and the output.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features:

- Collects detailed statistics, providing strong confidence that changes to performance are real, not measurement noise.
- Produces detailed charts, providing thorough understanding of your code’s performance behavior.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [async_](https://docs.rs/async_executor/index.html)- executor
- This module defines a trait that can be used to plug in different Futures executors into Criterion.rs’ async benchmarking support.
- [measurement](https://docs.rs/measurement/index.html)
- This module defines a set of traits that can be used to plug different measurements (eg.
Unix’s Processor Time, CPU or GPU performance counters, etc.) into Criterion.rs. It also
includes the `WallTime`
- [profiler](https://docs.rs/profiler/index.html)
- This module provides an extension trait which allows in-process profilers
to be hooked into the `--profile-time`argument at compile-time. Users of out-of-process profilers such as perf don’t need to do anything special.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [criterion_](https://docs.rs/macro.criterion_group.html)- group
- Macro used to define a function group for the benchmark harness; see the
`criterion_main!`
- [criterion_](https://docs.rs/macro.criterion_main.html)- main
- Macro which expands to a benchmark harness.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Async](https://docs.rs/struct.AsyncBencher.html)- Bencher
- Async/await variant of `Bencher`
- [Bencher](https://docs.rs/struct.Bencher.html)
- Timer struct used to iterate a benchmarked function and measure the runtime.
- [Benchmark](https://docs.rs/struct.BenchmarkGroup.html)- Group
- Structure used to group together a set of related benchmarks, along with custom configuration settings for groups of benchmarks. All benchmarks performed using a benchmark group will be grouped together in the final report.
- [Benchmark](https://docs.rs/struct.BenchmarkId.html)- Id
- Simple structure representing an ID for a benchmark. The ID must be unique within a benchmark group.
- [Criterion](https://docs.rs/struct.Criterion.html)
- The benchmark manager
- [Plot](https://docs.rs/struct.PlotConfiguration.html)- Configuration
- Contains the configuration options for the plots generated by a particular benchmark or benchmark group.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Axis](https://docs.rs/enum.AxisScale.html)- Scale
- Axis scaling type. Specified via `PlotConfiguration::summary_scale`
- [Baseline](https://docs.rs/enum.Baseline.html)
- Baseline describes how the `baseline_directory`is handled.
- [Batch](https://docs.rs/enum.BatchSize.html)- Size
- Argument to `Bencher::iter_batched``Bencher::iter_batched_ref`
- [Benchmark](https://docs.rs/enum.BenchmarkFilter.html)- Filter
- Benchmark filtering support.
- [Plotting](https://docs.rs/enum.PlottingBackend.html)- Backend
- Enum used to select the plotting backend.
- [Sampling](https://docs.rs/enum.SamplingMode.html)- Mode
- This enum allows the user to control how Criterion.rs chooses the iteration count when sampling.
The default is `Auto`, which will choose a method automatically based on the iteration time during the warm-up phase.
- [Throughput](https://docs.rs/enum.Throughput.html)
- Enum representing different ways of measuring the throughput of benchmarked code. If the throughput setting is configured for a benchmark then the estimated throughput will be reported as well as the time per iteration.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [black_](https://docs.rs/fn.black_box.html)- box - Deprecated
- A function that is opaque to the optimizer, used to prevent the compiler from optimizing away computations in a benchmark.

# quickcheck - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/quickcheck/^1/

## Expand description

This crate is a port of
[Haskell’s QuickCheck](https://hackage.haskell.org/package/QuickCheck).

QuickCheck is a library for random testing of program properties. The programmer provides a specification of the program, in the form of properties which functions should satisfy, and QuickCheck then tests that the properties hold in a large number of randomly generated cases.

For detailed examples, please see the
[README](https://github.com/BurntSushi/quickcheck).

[§](https://docs.rs#compatibility)Compatibility

In general, this crate considers the `Arbitrary` implementations provided as
implementation details. Strategies may or may not change over time, which may
cause new test failures, presumably due to the discovery of new bugs due to a
new kind of witness being generated. These sorts of changes may happen in
semver compatible releases.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [quickcheck](https://docs.rs/macro.quickcheck.html)
- A macro for writing quickcheck tests.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Gen](https://docs.rs/struct.Gen.html)
- `Gen`represents a PRNG.
- [NoShrink](https://docs.rs/struct.NoShrink.html)
- Wrapper for disabling shrinking for an Arbitrary
- [Quick](https://docs.rs/struct.QuickCheck.html)- Check
- The main `QuickCheck`type for setting configuration and running`QuickCheck`.
- [Test](https://docs.rs/struct.TestResult.html)- Result
- Describes the status of a single instance of a test.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Arbitrary](https://docs.rs/trait.Arbitrary.html)
- `Arbitrary`describes types whose values can be randomly generated and shrunk.
- [Testable](https://docs.rs/trait.Testable.html)
- `Testable`describes types (e.g., a function) whose values can be tested.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [empty_](https://docs.rs/fn.empty_shrinker.html)- shrinker
- Creates a shrinker with zero elements.
- [quickcheck](https://docs.rs/fn.quickcheck.html)
- Convenience function for running `QuickCheck`.
- [single_](https://docs.rs/fn.single_shrinker.html)- shrinker
- Creates a shrinker with a single element.

# rand - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rand/^0.9/

## Expand description

Utilities for random number generation

Rand provides utilities to generate random numbers, to convert them to useful types and distributions, and some randomness-related algorithms.

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

```
// The prelude import enables methods we use below, specifically
// Rng::random, Rng::sample, SliceRandom::shuffle and IndexedRandom::choose.
use rand::prelude::*;
// Get an RNG:
let mut rng = rand::rng();
// Try printing a random unicode code point (probably a bad idea)!
println!("char: '{}'", rng.random::<char>());
// Try printing a random alphanumeric value instead!
println!("alpha: '{}'", rng.sample(rand::distr::Alphanumeric) as char);
// Generate and shuffle a sequence:
let mut nums: Vec<i32> = (1..100).collect();
nums.shuffle(&mut rng);
// And take a random pick (yes, we didn't need to shuffle first!):
let _ = nums.choose(&mut rng);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#the-book)The Book

For the user guide and further documentation, please read
[The Rust Rand Book](https://rust-random.github.io/book).

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [rand_core](https://docs.rs/rand_core/0.9.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/rand_core/index.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [distr](https://docs.rs/distr/index.html)
- Generating random samples from probability distributions
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- Convenience re-export of common members
- [rngs](https://docs.rs/rngs/index.html)
- Random number generators and adapters
- [seq](https://docs.rs/seq/index.html)
- Sequence-related functionality

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Crypto](https://docs.rs/trait.CryptoRng.html)- Rng
- A marker trait over `RngCore`
- [Fill](https://docs.rs/trait.Fill.html)
- Types which may be filled with random data
- [Rng](https://docs.rs/trait.Rng.html)
- User-level interface for RNGs
- [RngCore](https://docs.rs/trait.RngCore.html)
- Implementation-level interface for RNGs
- [Seedable](https://docs.rs/trait.SeedableRng.html)- Rng
- A random number generator that can be explicitly seeded.
- [TryCrypto](https://docs.rs/trait.TryCryptoRng.html)- Rng
- A marker trait over `TryRngCore`
- [TryRng](https://docs.rs/trait.TryRngCore.html)- Core
- A potentially fallible variant of `RngCore`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [fill](https://docs.rs/fn.fill.html)- `thread_rng`
- Fill any type implementing `Fill`
- [random](https://docs.rs/fn.random.html)- `thread_rng`
- Generate a random value using the thread-local random number generator.
- [random_](https://docs.rs/fn.random_bool.html)- bool - `thread_rng`
- Return a bool with a probability `p`of being true.
- [random_](https://docs.rs/fn.random_iter.html)- iter - `thread_rng`
- Return an iterator over `random()`
- [random_](https://docs.rs/fn.random_range.html)- range - `thread_rng`
- Generate a random value in the given range using the thread-local random number generator.
- [random_](https://docs.rs/fn.random_ratio.html)- ratio - `thread_rng`
- Return a bool with a probability of `numerator/denominator`of being true.
- [rng](https://docs.rs/fn.rng.html)- `thread_rng`
- Access a fast, pre-initialized generator
- [thread_](https://docs.rs/fn.thread_rng.html)- rng - Deprecated - `thread_rng`
- Access the thread-local generator

- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the standard digit ordering (0 to 9, then A to Z, then a to z), and writes it to the passed buffer.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_fmt.html)- fmt
- Writes the base62 representation of a number using the standard alphabet to any fmt::Write destination.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_fmt_alt.html)- fmt_ - alt
- Writes the base62 representation of a number using the alternative alphabet to any fmt::Write destination.

# base62 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/base62/latest/target-redirect/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/base62/

## Expand description

`base62` is a `no_std` crate that provides base62 encoding and decoding functionality.

With the `alloc` feature (enabled by default), it provides functions for converting
between `u128` values and base62 strings using both standard (0-9, A-Z, a-z) and
alternative (0-9, a-z, A-Z) alphabets.

When used without default features, it provides the core encoding and decoding primitives that operate on byte slices.

For usage with the standard library’s IO traits, enable the `std` feature.

- [Decode](https://docs.rs/enum.DecodeError.html)- Error

- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_alternative.html)- alternative
- Decodes a base62 byte slice or an equivalent, like a `String`, using the alternative digit ordering (0 to 9, then a to z, then A to Z) with lowercase letters before uppercase letters.
- [encode](https://docs.rs/fn.encode.html)
- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the standard digit ordering
(0 to 9, then A to Z, then a to z), and returns the resulting
`String`

- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the alternative digit ordering

and returns the resulting `String`
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_alternative_buf.html)- alternative_ - buf
- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the alternative digit ordering
(0 to 9, then a to z, then A to Z) with lowercase letters before uppercase letters, and
then appends it onto the end of the given `String`

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

---

# Badges

Source: https://docs.rs/about/badges

Docs.rs no longer has its own badges. Consider using [shields.io](https://shields.io) instead.

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (4c9d2bfe4 2026-07-01)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

---

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# ankurah_signals - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ankurah-signals/0.8.1/ankurah_signals/

## Expand description

A signals library designed to support Ankurah’s needs - but can be used independently as well. Supports both native Rust and WebAssembly/React use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#basic-usage-in-rust)Basic Usage in Rust

```
let day = Mut::new("Friday");
let vibe = Mut::new("grindcore");
// Sometimes directly subscribing to the signal can be useful
// your listener will not be called immediately, only when the signal changes
// the subscription will be removed when the SubscriptionGuard is dropped
let _guard1 = day.subscribe(|v| println!("The day is: {}", v));
let _guard2 = vibe.subscribe(|v| println!("Vibe: {}", v));
// For things that need to track signal dependencies, we can use an Observer
let renderer = {
    let day = day.read(); // Read<T> signals can be constructed from a Mut<T> signal
    let vibe = vibe.read();
    CallbackObserver::new(Arc::new(move ||{
        // Your "render" function that uses signals
        // The Observer will automatically subscribe to the signals used
        // during this dispatch using the thread-local CurrentObserver
        println!("It's {day} and I'm {vibe}") // the Observer will automatically subscribe to the signals
    }))
};
renderer.trigger(); // trigger the initial "render". Signals used will be tracked by the observer.
// Should print:
// It's Friday and I'm grindcore
vibe.set("chillmaxing"); // triggers the direct signal subscription AND the observer
// Should print:
// Vibe: chillmaxing
// It's Friday and I'm chillmaxing
day.set("Saturday");
// Should print:
// The day is: Saturday
// It's Saturday and I'm chillmaxing
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use broadcast::`- [BroadcastId](https://docs.rs/broadcast/struct.BroadcastId.html);
- `pub use`- [observer](https://docs.rs/observer/index.html)::*;
- `pub use`- [porcelain](https://docs.rs/porcelain/index.html)::*;
- `pub use`- [signal](https://docs.rs/signal/index.html)::*;
- `pub use`- [reactive_graph](https://docs.rs/reactive_graph/index.html)::*;

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [broadcast](https://docs.rs/broadcast/index.html)
- [observer](https://docs.rs/observer/index.html)
- [porcelain](https://docs.rs/porcelain/index.html)
- [reactive_](https://docs.rs/reactive_graph/index.html)- graph
- ReactiveGraphObserver: low-road integration with Leptos / reactive_graph.
- [signal](https://docs.rs/signal/index.html)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Current](https://docs.rs/struct.CurrentObserver.html)- Observer
- Manages the current observer stack and provides a way to subscribe the current observer to a given signal

# dent8_store_sqlite - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/dent8-store-sqlite/0.1.0/dent8_store_sqlite/

## Expand description

Embedded `SQLite` adapter for the dent8 event log — the second async backend, and the proof
that the storage boundary is backend-agnostic.

It implements [ dent8_store::AsyncEventStore](https://docs.rs/dent8-store/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/dent8_store/trait.AsyncEventStore.html) over a single append-only table, reusing the

*same*pure firewall decision as every other backend (

[) and the same canonical](https://docs.rs/dent8-store/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/dent8_store/firewall/fn.arbitrate_events.html)

`dent8_store::arbitrate_events`[/](https://docs.rs/dent8-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/dent8_core/hash/fn.event_hash.html)

`event_hash`[. Where it differs from the Postgres adapter is only the](https://docs.rs/dent8-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/dent8_core/hash/fn.hash_chain.html)

`hash_chain`**primitives**, exactly as a second backend should:

- storage is **embedded**(a file or`:memory:`, no server, bundled libsqlite3);
- writers **serialize via**(the write lock is taken up front, before the chain-head read), with WAL for reader concurrency — so concurrent writers`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`+`busy_timeout`*wait*rather than fail, and a residual busy past the timeout is surfaced as a retryable`Conflict`(the analogue of Postgres’ advisory lock + optimistic-id retry);
- the canonical event is stored as **TEXT**(`event_json`), since`SQLite`has no`JSONB`.

v0 is lean: the event log only. The believed projection is folded from the log on read (the
`projection == fold(log)` invariant), like the in-memory/file backend — the materialized
caches the Postgres adapter keeps (migration 003) are a possible later addition. The
per-event append *algorithm* (arbitrate → dedup → chain → insert) is structurally the same
as Postgres’; only the SQL dialect is `SQLite`-native (so Postgres assumptions cannot leak).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Sqlite](https://docs.rs/struct.SqliteEventStore.html)- Event - Store
- A v0 `SQLite`-backed event store. The pool is capped at**one connection**: that serializes writers*within*a process (cross-process serialization is`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`+`busy_timeout`in`Self::append_many``:memory:`database alive for the pool’s lifetime.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [SCHEMA_](https://docs.rs/constant.SCHEMA_SQL.html)- SQL
- The v0 append-only event-log schema. Mirrors the Postgres `dent8_event_log`(migration 002) minus the materialized caches:`event_json`is TEXT (no`JSONB`),`global_sequence`is the`SQLite`rowid.

# ankql - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ankql/0.8.1/ankql/

## Expand description

Ankql intends to be query language for Ankurah in the style of Open Cypher and GQL (ISO/IEC 39075:2024), but is sort of just sql because it’s only used for selection right now. The point of this is not to reinvent the wheel, but to provide a fast-to-implement query language for Ankurah which has only the necessary features to be useful.

If this pans out, we might someday consider a more complete implementation and ISO/IEC 39075:2024 compliance.

# system_utils - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/system-utils/0.1.0/system_utils/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#system-utilities)System Utilities

Cross-platform utilities for interacting with operating system features such as audio control, power management, system information, hardware monitoring, and device enumeration.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features:

- Audio management
- Power actions with optional timers
- System information
- Real-time system metrics monitoring
- Hardware device enumeration
- Cross-platform API (Windows, Linux, macOS where supported)

[§](https://docs.rs#installation)Installation

`cargo add system-utils --features full`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples:

[§](https://docs.rs#system-monitoring-feature-monitor)System Monitoring [feature `monitor`]:

`SystemMonitor` caches system information, metrics, and device lists internally.
Calling `refresh_*_with_interval()` updates the cached data only if the specified interval has elapsed,
reducing unnecessary operating system queries.

```
use system_utils::SystemMonitor;
use tokio::time::Duration;
fn main() {
    let mut monitor = SystemMonitor::default();
    // static system information (cached forever)
    let info = monitor.info();
    println!("{info}");
    // collect current system metrics
    let metrics = monitor.refresh_metrics_with_interval(Duration::from_secs(10));
    println!("{metrics}");
    // enumerate connected devices
    let devices = monitor.refresh_devices_with_interval(Duration::from_secs(60));
    println!("{devices}")
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#basic-system-info-feature-info)Basic System Info [feature `info`]:

```
use system_utils::SystemInfo;
fn main() {
    // create a snapshot of the current system information
    let info = SystemInfo::new();
    println!("{info}");
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#system-metrics-feature-metrics)System Metrics [feature `metrics`]:

`SystemMetrics::new()` collects a complete snapshot of the current system state, including CPU, GPU, memory, disks, network interfaces,
proxy configuration, battery information (when available), and system uptime.
The returned snapshot is immutable and represents the system state at the moment it was created.

```
use system_utils::SystemMetrics;
fn main() {
    // collect a snapshot of the current system metrics
    let metrics = SystemMetrics::new();
    println!("{metrics}");
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#devices-list-feature-devices)Devices List [feature `devices`]:

`DevicesList::new()` creates a snapshot of the currently connected hardware devices, including monitors, audio devices, cameras, and USB devices.
The snapshot is immutable and reflects the hardware state at the time it was created.

```
use system_utils::DevicesList;
fn main() {
    // enumerate connected hardware devices
    let devices = DevicesList::new();
    println!("{devices}");
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#audio-control-feature-audio)Audio Control [feature `audio`]:

`SystemAudio` provides a cross-platform API for controlling the system master volume.
It supports getting and setting the volume, increasing or decreasing it by a delta, and muting or unmuting the default audio output device.

```
use system_utils::AudioControl;
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<()> {
    // get the current master volume
    let volume = AudioControl::get_volume().await?;
    println!("Current volume: {}%", volume);
    // increase the volume by 10%
    let volume = AudioControl::increase_volume(10).await?;
    println!("Volume: {}%", volume);
    // decrease the volume by 5%
    let volume = AudioControl::decrease_volume(5).await?;
    println!("Volume: {}%", volume);
    // set an exact volume level
    AudioControl::set_volume(50).await?;
    // mute / unmute
    if !AudioControl::is_muted().await? {
        AudioControl::set_mute(true).await?;
        println!("Audio muted.");
    }
    AudioControl::set_mute(false).await?;
    println!("Audio restored.");
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#power-management-feature-power)Power Management [feature `power`]:

`SystemPower` provides cross-platform power management, including shutdown, reboot, suspend, lock, and logout operations.
Every action can be executed immediately or scheduled for a future `DateTime<Utc>`.
Only one scheduled power action can be active at a time; scheduling a new action automatically replaces the previous one.

```
use chrono::{Duration, Utc};
use system_utils::PowerManager;
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<()> {
    // schedule a shutdown in 5 minutes
    let execute_at = Utc::now() + Duration::minutes(5);
    PowerManager::shutdown(Some(execute_at)).await?;
    // check the scheduled task
    if let Some(task) = PowerManager::status().await {
        println!(
            "{:?} scheduled for {}",
            task.mode,
            task.execute_at
        );
    }
    // cancel the scheduled action
    if PowerManager::cancel().await {
        println!("Scheduled power action cancelled.");
    }
    // execute an action immediately
    // PowerManager::lock_now().await?;
    // PowerManager::logout_now().await?;
    // PowerManager::reboot_now().await?;
    // PowerManager::shutdown_now().await?;
    // PowerManager::suspend_now().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#license--feedback)License & Feedback:

Distributed under the

[MIT](https://github.com/fuderis/system-utils-rs/blob/main/LICENSE.md)license.

You can contact me via [GitHub](https://github.com/fuderis) or send a message to my [E-Mail](mailto:synapdrake@ya.ru).
This library is actively evolving, and your suggestions and feedback are always welcome!

# daemon - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/marshal-daemon/0.20.0/daemon/

## Expand description

Daemon-side library code: cleanup sweeper, auto-room saga, and the on-disk event persister.

`link()` is called from the bin to ensure the `inventory` registrations
generated by `#[myko_saga]` / `#[myko_command]` survive dead-code
elimination. Message delivery itself is handled directly by the
`marshal_entities::SendMessage` and `marshal_entities::BroadcastMessage`
commands — there’s no saga in the critical path for delivery.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [auto_](https://docs.rs/auto_rooms/index.html)- rooms
- Daemon-side reactive auto-room maintenance.
- [cleanup](https://docs.rs/cleanup/index.html)
- Periodic sweep that DELs abandoned sessions.
- [hooks](https://docs.rs/hooks/index.html)
- Claude Code hook logic — all of it server-side.
- [http_](https://docs.rs/http_listener/index.html)- listener
- marshal’s own minimal plain-HTTP listener for the Claude Code
`/hook/*`endpoints.
- [persister](https://docs.rs/persister/index.html)
- Append-only JSONL disk persister.

# ddd_cqrs_es - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ddd_cqrs_es/0.2.3/ddd_cqrs_es/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#ddd_cqrs_es)ddd_cqrs_es

A lightweight framework for building Domain-Driven Design, CQRS, and Event Sourcing applications in Rust.

The crate provides explicit building blocks for aggregate command handling, optimistic concurrency, event replay, projections, process managers, snapshots, and pluggable persistence backends. The included in-memory store is intended for tests, examples, and local development.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use ddd_cqrs_es::{Aggregate, DomainEvent, InMemoryEventStore, Metadata, Repository};
#[derive(Clone)]
enum CounterEvent {
    Created,
    Incremented(u64),
}
impl DomainEvent for CounterEvent {
    fn event_type(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            CounterEvent::Created => "counter_created",
            CounterEvent::Incremented(_) => "counter_incremented",
        }
    }
}
enum CounterCommand {
    Create,
    Increment(u64),
}
#[derive(Default)]
struct Counter {
    exists: bool,
    value: u64,
    revision: u64,
}
#[derive(Debug)]
enum CounterError {
    AlreadyCreated,
    NotCreated,
}
impl Aggregate for Counter {
    type Id = String;
    type Command = CounterCommand;
    type Event = CounterEvent;
    type Error = CounterError;
    fn aggregate_type() -> &'static str { "counter" }
    fn revision(&self) -> u64 { self.revision }
    fn new() -> Self { Self::default() }
    fn apply(&mut self, event: &Self::Event) {
        match event {
            CounterEvent::Created => self.exists = true,
            CounterEvent::Incremented(by) => self.value += by,
        }
        self.revision += 1;
    }
    fn handle(&self, command: Self::Command) -> Result<Vec<Self::Event>, Self::Error> {
        match command {
            CounterCommand::Create if self.exists => Err(CounterError::AlreadyCreated),
            CounterCommand::Create => Ok(vec![CounterEvent::Created]),
            CounterCommand::Increment(_) if !self.exists => Err(CounterError::NotCreated),
            CounterCommand::Increment(by) => Ok(vec![CounterEvent::Incremented(by)]),
        }
    }
}
let store = InMemoryEventStore::<Counter>::new();
let repo = Repository::new(store);
let counter_id = "counter-1".to_owned();
repo.execute(&counter_id, CounterCommand::Create, Metadata::default())?;
repo.execute(&counter_id, CounterCommand::Increment(5), Metadata::default())?;
let loaded = repo.load(&counter_id)?;
assert_eq!(loaded.state.value, 5);
```

# base62 2.2.4 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/base62/2.2.4

# base62

A fast, zero-dependency base62 encoder/decoder library for Rust, typically used in URL shorteners. It supports both standard [0-9A-Za-z] and alternative [0-9a-zA-Z] variants.

## Features

- `no_std`compatible with optional- `alloc`and- `std`support
- Encodes integers up to `u128`
- Zero-copy decoding
- Efficient string handling
- Two encoding variants:
- Standard [0-9A-Za-z]
- Alternative [0-9a-zA-Z]

## Usage

Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "2"
```
### Basic Example

```
use base62;
// Encoding
let encoded = encode;
assert_eq!;
// Decoding
let decoded = decode.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
```
### No-std Usage

The crate works in `no_std` environments by default:

```
use base62;
// Encode into a fixed buffer
let mut buf = ;  // Maximum size needed for u128
let len = encode_bytes.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
// Decode from bytes
let decoded = decode.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
```
## Feature Flags

- `alloc`: Enables String allocation support (enabled by default)
- `std`: Enables std::io traits support

## Performance

The library is optimized for both encoding and decoding performance:

- Zero-copy decoding
- Efficient buffer management
- Direct string manipulation for optimal performance when appending

## License

Licensed under the MIT license. See LICENSE for details.

---

                    base62 2.2.4

# base62 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/base62/2.2.4/target-redirect/aarch64-apple-darwin/base62/

## Expand description

`base62` is a `no_std` crate that provides base62 encoding and decoding functionality.

With the `alloc` feature (enabled by default), it provides functions for converting
between `u128` values and base62 strings using both standard (0-9, A-Z, a-z) and
alternative (0-9, a-z, A-Z) alphabets.

When used without default features, it provides the core encoding and decoding primitives that operate on byte slices.

For usage with the standard library’s IO traits, enable the `std` feature.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Decode](https://docs.rs/enum.DecodeError.html)- Error
- Indicates the cause of a decoding failure in base62 decoding operations.
- [Encode](https://docs.rs/enum.EncodeError.html)- Error
- Indicates the cause of an encoding failure in encoding operations.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [decode](https://docs.rs/fn.decode.html)
- Decodes a base62 byte slice or an equivalent, like a `String`, using the standard digit ordering (0 to 9, then A to Z, then a to z).
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_alternative.html)- alternative
- Decodes a base62 byte slice or an equivalent, like a `String`, using the alternative digit ordering (0 to 9, then a to z, then A to Z) with lowercase letters before uppercase letters.
- [encode](https://docs.rs/fn.encode.html)
- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the standard digit ordering
(0 to 9, then A to Z, then a to z), and returns the resulting
`String`
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_alternative.html)- alternative
- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the alternative digit ordering
(0 to 9, then a to z, then A to Z) with lowercase letters before uppercase letters,
and returns the resulting `String`
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_alternative_buf.html)- alternative_ - buf
- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the alternative digit ordering
(0 to 9, then a to z, then A to Z) with lowercase letters before uppercase letters, and
then appends it onto the end of the given `String`
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_alternative_bytes.html)- alternative_ - bytes
- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the alternative digit ordering (0 to 9, then a to z, then A to Z), and writes it to the passed buffer.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_buf.html)- buf
- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the standard digit ordering
(0 to 9, then A to Z, then a to z), and then appends it onto the end of the given
`String`
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_bytes.html)- bytes
- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the standard digit ordering (0 to 9, then A to Z, then a to z), and writes it to the passed buffer.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_fmt.html)- fmt
- Writes the base62 representation of a number using the standard alphabet to any fmt::Write destination.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_fmt_alt.html)- fmt_ - alt
- Writes the base62 representation of a number using the alternative alphabet to any fmt::Write destination.

---

and returns the resulting `String`
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_alternative_buf.html)- alternative_ - buf
- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the alternative digit ordering
(0 to 9, then a to z, then A to Z) with lowercase letters before uppercase letters, and
then appends it onto the end of the given `String`
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_alternative_bytes.html)- alternative_ - bytes
- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the alternative digit ordering (0 to 9, then a to z, then A to Z), and writes it to the passed buffer.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_buf.html)- buf
- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the standard digit ordering
(0 to 9, then A to Z, then a to z), and then appends it onto the end of the given
`String`
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_bytes.html)- bytes
- Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the standard digit ordering (0 to 9, then A to Z, then a to z), and writes it to the passed buffer.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_fmt.html)- fmt
- Writes the base62 representation of a number using the standard alphabet to any fmt::Write destination.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_fmt_alt.html)- fmt_ - alt
- Writes the base62 representation of a number using the alternative alphabet to any fmt::Write destination.

---

[64](#64)impl StandardTables {
[65](#65)    const fn new() -> Self {
[66](#66)        const ENCODE: [u8; 62] = [
[68](#68)            b'0', b'1', b'2', b'3', b'4', b'5', b'6', b'7', b'8', b'9', b'A', b'B', b'C', b'D',
[69](#69)            b'E', b'F', b'G', b'H', b'I', b'J', b'K', b'L', b'M', b'N', b'O', b'P', b'Q', b'R',
[70](#70)            b'S', b'T', b'U', b'V', b'W', b'X', b'Y', b'Z', b'a', b'b', b'c', b'd', b'e', b'f',
[71](#71)            b'g', b'h', b'i', b'j', b'k', b'l', b'm', b'n', b'o', b'p', b'q', b'r', b's', b't',
[72](#72)            b'u', b'v', b'w', b'x', b'y', b'z',
[73](#73)        ];
[74](#74)
[75](#75)        let mut encode_pairs = [[0u8; 2]; BASE_TO_2 as usize];
[77](#77)        let mut i = 0usize;
[78](#78)        while i < BASE_TO_2 as usize {
[79](#79)            let hi = i / 62;
[80](#80)            let lo = i % 62;
[81](#81)            encode_pairs[i] = [ENCODE[hi], ENCODE[lo]];
[82](#82)            i += 1;
[83](#83)        }
[84](#84)
[85](#85)        let mut decode = [255u8; 128];
[86](#86)
[87](#87)        let mut i = 0u8;
[89](#89)        while i < 10 {
[90](#90)            decode[(b'0' + i) as usize] = i;
[91](#91)            i += 1;
[92](#92)        }
[93](#93)        let mut i = 0u8;
[94](#94)        while i < 26 {
[95](#95)            decode[(b'A' + i) as usize] = i + 10;
[96](#96)            i += 1;
[97](#97)        }
[98](#98)        let mut i = 0u8;
[99](#99)        while i < 26 {
[100](#100)            decode[(b'a' + i) as usize] = i + 36;
[101](#101)            i += 1;
[102](#102)        }
[103](#103)
[104](#104)        Self {
[105](#105)            encode_pairs,
[106](#106)            decode,
[107](#107)        }
[108](#108)    }
[109](#109)}

[178](#178)impl fmt::Display for DecodeError {
[179](#179)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
[180](#180)        match *self {
[181](#181)            DecodeError::ArithmeticOverflow => {
[182](#182)                f.write_str("Decoded number cannot fit into a `u128`")
[183](#183)            }
[184](#184)            DecodeError::EmptyInput => f.write_str("Encoded input is an empty string"),
[185](#185)            DecodeError::InvalidBase62Byte(ch, idx) => {
[186](#186)                use fmt::Write;
[187](#187)                f.write_str("Encoded input contains the invalid byte b'")?;
[188](#188)                for char_in_escape in core::ascii::escape_default(ch) {
[189](#189)                    f.write_char(char::from(char_in_escape))?;
[190](#190)                }
[191](#191)                write!(f, "' at index {idx}")
[192](#192)            }
[193](#193)        }
[194](#194)    }

[341](#341)
[342](#342)pub(crate) fn digit_count(n: u128) -> usize {
[344](#344)    const THRESHOLDS: [u128; 23] = [
[345](#345)        0,
[346](#346)        BASE as u128 - 1,
[347](#347)        BASE_TO_2 as u128 - 1,
[348](#348)        BASE_TO_3 as u128 - 1,
[349](#349)        BASE_TO_4 as u128 - 1,
[350](#350)        BASE_TO_5 as u128 - 1,
[351](#351)        BASE_TO_6 as u128 - 1,
[352](#352)        BASE_TO_7 as u128 - 1,
[353](#353)        BASE_TO_8 as u128 - 1,
[354](#354)        BASE_TO_9 as u128 - 1,
[355](#355)        BASE_TO_10 - 1,
[356](#356)        BASE_TO_11 - 1,
[357](#357)        BASE_TO_12 - 1,
[358](#358)        BASE_TO_13 - 1,
[359](#359)        BASE_TO_14 - 1,
[360](#360)        BASE_TO_15 - 1,
[361](#361)        BASE_TO_16 - 1,
[362](#362)        BASE_TO_17 - 1,
[363](#363)        BASE_TO_18 - 1,
[364](#364)        BASE_TO_19 - 1,
[365](#365)        BASE_TO_20 - 1,
[366](#366)        BASE_TO_21 - 1,
[367](#367)        u128::MAX, ];
[369](#369)
[370](#370)    let Some(n) = NonZeroU128::new(n) else {
[371](#371)        return 1;
[372](#372)    };
[373](#373)    let ilog2 = n.ilog2() as usize;
[376](#376)
[377](#377)    let estimate = ((ilog2 * 43) >> 8) + 1;
[380](#380)
[381](#381)    let threshold = unsafe { *THRESHOLDS.get_unchecked(estimate) };
[383](#383)    let bump = (n.get() > threshold) as usize;
[384](#384)    estimate + bump
[385](#385)}
[386](#386)
[387](#387)#[inline(always)]
[388](#388)fn decode_char(
[389](#389)    result: &mut u64,
[390](#390)    ch: u8,
[391](#391)    i: usize,
[392](#392)    decode_table: &[u8; 128],
[393](#393)) -> Result<(), DecodeError> {
[394](#394)    if ch < 128 {
[395](#395)        let char_value = decode_table[ch as usize];
[396](#396)
[397](#397)        let is_valid = (char_value != 255) as u64;
[399](#399)        *result = result
[400](#400)            .wrapping_mul(BASE)
[401](#401)            .wrapping_add((char_value as u64) * is_valid);
[402](#402)
[403](#403)        if char_value == 255 {
[404](#404)            Err(DecodeError::InvalidBase62Byte(ch, i))
[405](#405)        } else {
[406](#406)            Ok(())
[407](#407)        }
[408](#408)    } else {
[409](#409)        Err(DecodeError::InvalidBase62Byte(ch, i))
[411](#411)    }
[412](#412)}
[413](#413)
[414](#414)#[inline]
[416](#416)fn decode_impl(mut input: &[u8], decode_table: &[u8; 128]) -> Result<u128, DecodeError> {
[417](#417)    if input.is_empty() {
[418](#418)        return Err(DecodeError::EmptyInput);
[419](#419)    }
[420](#420)
[421](#421)    let chopped_count = input.iter().take_while(|&&ch| ch == b'0').count();
[423](#423)    input = &input[chopped_count..];
[424](#424)
[425](#425)    let input_len = input.len();
[426](#426)    if input_len <= 22 {
[427](#427)        const MULTIPLIERS: [(u128, u64); 23] = [
[428](#428)            (0, 0),
[429](#429)            (1, 1),
[430](#430)            (1, 1),
[431](#431)            (1, 1),
[432](#432)            (1, 1),
[433](#433)            (1, 1),
[434](#434)            (1, 1),
[435](#435)            (1, 1),
[436](#436)            (1, 1),
[437](#437)            (1, 1),
[438](#438)            (1, 1),
[439](#439)            (BASE as u128, 1),
[440](#440)            (BASE_TO_2 as u128, 1),
[441](#441)            (BASE_TO_3 as u128, 1),
[442](#442)            (BASE_TO_4 as u128, 1),
[443](#443)            (BASE_TO_5 as u128, 1),
[444](#444)            (BASE_TO_6 as u128, 1),
[445](#445)            (BASE_TO_7 as u128, 1),
[446](#446)            (BASE_TO_8 as u128, 1),
[447](#447)            (BASE_TO_9 as u128, 1),
[448](#448)            (BASE_TO_10, 1),
[449](#449)            (BASE_TO_11, BASE),
[450](#450)            (BASE_TO_12, BASE_TO_2),
[451](#451)        ];
[452](#452)
[453](#453)        let (a_power, b_power) = MULTIPLIERS[input_len];
[454](#454)
[455](#455)        let mut iter = (chopped_count..).zip(input.iter().copied());
[456](#456)
[457](#457)        let mut result_a = 0_u64;
[459](#459)        for (i, ch) in iter.by_ref().take(10) {
[460](#460)            decode_char(&mut result_a, ch, i, decode_table)?;
[461](#461)        }
[462](#462)        let result_a = (result_a as u128)
[463](#463)            .checked_mul(a_power)
[464](#464)            .ok_or(DecodeError::ArithmeticOverflow)?;
[465](#465)
[466](#466)        let mut result_b = 0_u64;
[468](#468)        for (i, ch) in iter.by_ref().take(10) {
[469](#469)            decode_char(&mut result_b, ch, i, decode_table)?;
[470](#470)        }
[471](#471)        let result_b = (result_b as u128).wrapping_mul(b_power as u128);
[472](#472)
[473](#473)        let mut result_c = 0_u64;
[475](#475)        for (i, ch) in iter {
[476](#476)            decode_char(&mut result_c, ch, i, decode_table)?;
[477](#477)        }
[478](#478)        let result_c = result_c as u128;
[479](#479)
[480](#480)        let result = result_a
[481](#481)            .checked_add(result_b.wrapping_add(result_c))
[482](#482)            .ok_or(DecodeError::ArithmeticOverflow)?;
[483](#483)        Ok(result)
[484](#484)    } else {
[485](#485)        Err(DecodeError::ArithmeticOverflow)
[486](#486)    }
[487](#487)}
[488](#488)
[489](#489)pub fn encode_bytes<T: Into<u128>>(num: T, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, EncodeError> {
[511](#511)    let num = num.into();
[512](#512)    let digits = digit_count(num);
[513](#513)
[514](#514)    if buf.len() < digits {
[515](#515)        return Err(EncodeError::BufferTooSmall);
[516](#516)    }
[517](#517)
[518](#518)    unsafe {
[519](#519)        let len = _encode_buf(num, digits, &mut buf[..digits]);
[520](#520)        debug_assert_eq!(len, digits);
[521](#521)    }
[522](#522)
[523](#523)    Ok(digits)
[524](#524)}

[555](#555)        return Err(EncodeError::BufferTooSmall);
[556](#556)    }
[557](#557)
[558](#558)    unsafe {
[559](#559)        let len = _encode_alternative_buf(num, digits, &mut buf[..digits]);
[560](#560)        debug_assert_eq!(len, digits);
[561](#561)    }
[562](#562)
[563](#563)    Ok(digits)

[566](#566)pub fn decode<T: AsRef<[u8]>>(input: T) -> Result<u128, DecodeError> {
[581](#581)    decode_impl(input.as_ref(), &STANDARD_TABLES.decode)
[582](#582)}
[583](#583)
[584](#584)pub fn decode_alternative<T: AsRef<[u8]>>(input: T) -> Result<u128, DecodeError> {
[600](#600)    decode_impl(input.as_ref(), &ALTERNATIVE_TABLES.decode)
[601](#601)}
[602](#602)
[603](#603)unsafe fn encode_impl(
[605](#605)    num: u128,
[606](#606)    digits: usize,
[607](#607)    buf: &mut [u8],
[608](#608)    encode_pairs: &[[u8; 2]; BASE_TO_2 as usize],
[609](#609)) -> usize {
[610](#610)    unsafe {
[611](#611)        if let Ok(num) = TryInto::<u64>::try_into(num) {
[612](#612)            encode_impl_u64(num, digits, buf, encode_pairs)
[613](#613)        } else if digits > 20 {
[614](#614)            encode_impl_over_20_digits(num, digits, buf, encode_pairs)
[615](#615)        } else if digits == 20 {
[616](#616)            let (first_u64, second_u64) = div_base_to_10(num);
[618](#618)            let first_u64 = first_u64 as u64;
[620](#620)
[621](#621)            encode_impl_20_digits(first_u64, second_u64, buf, encode_pairs)
[622](#622)        } else {
[623](#623)            encode_impl_over_10_under_20_digits(num, digits, buf, encode_pairs)
[625](#625)        }
[626](#626)    }
[627](#627)}
[628](#628)
[629](#629)unsafe fn encode_impl_over_20_digits(
[631](#631)    num: u128,
[632](#632)    digits: usize,
[633](#633)    buf: &mut [u8],
[634](#634)    encode_pairs: &[[u8; 2]; BASE_TO_2 as usize],
[635](#635)) -> usize {
[636](#636)    let (num, third_u64) = div_base_to_10(num);
[640](#640)    let (first_u64, second_u64) = div_base_to_10(num);
[642](#642)    let first_u64 = first_u64 as u64;
[644](#644)
[645](#645)    unsafe {
[649](#649)        let [c1, c2] = *encode_pairs.get_unchecked(first_u64 as usize);
[651](#651)        let is_22 = digits - 21; *buf.get_unchecked_mut(0) = c1;
[653](#653)        *buf.get_unchecked_mut(is_22) = c2;
[654](#654)    }
[655](#655)
[656](#656)    unsafe {
[658](#658)        encode_impl_20_digits(
[659](#659)            second_u64,
[660](#660)            third_u64,
[661](#661)            &mut buf[(digits - 20)..],
[662](#662)            encode_pairs,
[663](#663)        );
[664](#664)    }
[665](#665)
[666](#666)    digits
[667](#667)}
[668](#668)
[669](#669)unsafe fn encode_impl_20_digits(
[671](#671)    first_u64: u64,
[672](#672)    second_u64: u64,
[673](#673)    buf: &mut [u8],
[674](#674)    encode_pairs: &[[u8; 2]; BASE_TO_2 as usize],
[675](#675)) -> usize {
[676](#676)    let first_u32 = (first_u64 / BASE_TO_5) as u32;
[677](#677)    let second_u32 = (first_u64 % BASE_TO_5) as u32;
[678](#678)    let third_u32 = (second_u64 / BASE_TO_5) as u32;
[679](#679)    let fourth_u32 = (second_u64 % BASE_TO_5) as u32;
[680](#680)
[681](#681)    let mut nums = [first_u32, second_u32, third_u32, fourth_u32];
[683](#683)    const BASE_POSITIONS: [usize; 4] = [0, 5, 10, 15];
[684](#684)
[685](#685)    for pair_idx in 0..2 {
[686](#686)        nums.iter_mut().zip(BASE_POSITIONS).for_each(|(num, base)| {
[687](#687)            let quotient = *num / BASE_TO_2 as u32;
[690](#690)            let pair = (*num - BASE_TO_2 as u32 * quotient) as usize;
[693](#693)            *num = quotient;
[694](#694)
[695](#695)            let pos = base + 4 - 2 * pair_idx;
[697](#697)            unsafe {
[698](#698)                let [c1, c2] = *encode_pairs.get_unchecked(pair);
[701](#701)                *buf.get_unchecked_mut(pos - 1) = c1;
[702](#702)                *buf.get_unchecked_mut(pos) = c2;
[703](#703)            }
[704](#704)        });
[705](#705)    }
[706](#706)
[707](#707)    nums.iter()
[709](#709)        .zip(BASE_POSITIONS)
[710](#710)        .for_each(|(num, base)| unsafe {
[711](#711)            *buf.get_unchecked_mut(base) = encode_pairs.get_unchecked(*num as usize)[1];
[713](#713)        });
[714](#714)
[715](#715)    20
[716](#716)}
[717](#717)
[718](#718)unsafe fn encode_impl_over_10_under_20_digits(
[720](#720)    num: u128,
[721](#721)    digits: usize,
[722](#722)    buf: &mut [u8],
[723](#723)    encode_pairs: &[[u8; 2]; BASE_TO_2 as usize],
[724](#724)) -> usize {
[725](#725)    let mut write_idx = digits;
[726](#726)    let mut digit_index = 0_usize;
[727](#727)
[728](#728)    let (first_u64, mut num) = div_base_to_10(num);
[729](#729)    let first_u64 = first_u64 as u64;
[731](#731)
[732](#732)    while digit_index < digits {
[733](#733)        write_idx = write_idx.wrapping_sub(1);
[734](#734)
[735](#735)        let remainder = num % BASE;
[736](#736)        num /= BASE;
[737](#737)
[738](#738)        unsafe {
[739](#739)            *buf.get_unchecked_mut(write_idx) = encode_pairs.get_unchecked(remainder as usize)[1];
[740](#740)        }
[741](#741)
[742](#742)        digit_index = digit_index.wrapping_add(1);
[743](#743)        if digit_index == 10 {
[744](#744)            num = first_u64
[745](#745)        }
[746](#746)    }
[747](#747)
[748](#748)    digits
[749](#749)}
[750](#750)
[751](#751)unsafe fn encode_impl_u64(
[753](#753)    num: u64,
[754](#754)    digits: usize,
[755](#755)    buf: &mut [u8],
[756](#756)    encode_pairs: &[[u8; 2]; BASE_TO_2 as usize],
[757](#757)) -> usize {
[758](#758)    if digits >= 10 {
[759](#759)        let first_digit = num / (BASE_TO_10 as u64);
[763](#763)        let remainder = num % (BASE_TO_10 as u64);
[764](#764)        let offset = digits - 10; unsafe {
[767](#767)            *buf.get_unchecked_mut(0) = encode_pairs.get_unchecked(first_digit as usize)[1];
[769](#769)
[770](#770)            encode_impl_u64_10_digits(remainder, &mut buf[offset..], encode_pairs);
[771](#771)        }
[772](#772)        digits
[773](#773)    } else {
[774](#774)        unsafe { encode_impl_u64_under_10_digits(num, digits, buf, encode_pairs) }
[775](#775)    }
[776](#776)}
[777](#777)
[778](#778)unsafe fn encode_impl_u64_under_10_digits(
[779](#779)    mut num: u64,
[780](#780)    digits: usize,
[781](#781)    buf: &mut [u8],
[782](#782)    encode_pairs: &[[u8; 2]; BASE_TO_2 as usize],
[783](#783)) -> usize {
[784](#784)    let mut write_idx = digits;
[785](#785)    let mut digit_index = 0_usize;
[786](#786)
[787](#787)    while digit_index < digits {
[788](#788)        write_idx = write_idx.wrapping_sub(1);
[789](#789)
[790](#790)        let remainder = num % BASE;
[791](#791)        num /= BASE;
[792](#792)
[793](#793)        unsafe {
[794](#794)            *buf.get_unchecked_mut(write_idx) = encode_pairs.get_unchecked(remainder as usize)[1];
[795](#795)        }
[796](#796)
[797](#797)        digit_index = digit_index.wrapping_add(1);
[798](#798)    }
[799](#799)
[800](#800)    digits
[801](#801)}
[802](#802)
[803](#803)unsafe fn encode_impl_u64_10_digits(
[804](#804)    num: u64,
[805](#805)    buf: &mut [u8],
[806](#806)    encode_pairs: &[[u8; 2]; BASE_TO_2 as usize],
[807](#807)) -> usize {
[808](#808)    let first_u32 = (num / BASE_TO_5) as u32;
[809](#809)    let second_u32 = (num % BASE_TO_5) as u32;
[810](#810)
[811](#811)    let mut nums = [first_u32, second_u32];
[813](#813)    const BASE_POSITIONS: [usize; 2] = [0, 5];
[814](#814)
[815](#815)    for pair_idx in 0..2 {
[816](#816)        nums.iter_mut().zip(BASE_POSITIONS).for_each(|(num, base)| {
[817](#817)            let quotient = *num / BASE_TO_2 as u32;
[820](#820)            let pair = (*num - BASE_TO_2 as u32 * quotient) as usize;
[823](#823)            *num = quotient;
[824](#824)
[825](#825)            let pos = base + 4 - 2 * pair_idx;
[827](#827)            unsafe {
[828](#828)                let [c1, c2] = *encode_pairs.get_unchecked(pair);
[831](#831)                *buf.get_unchecked_mut(pos - 1) = c1;
[832](#832)                *buf.get_unchecked_mut(pos) = c2;
[833](#833)            }
[834](#834)        });
[835](#835)    }
[836](#836)
[837](#837)    nums.iter()
[839](#839)        .zip(BASE_POSITIONS)
[840](#840)        .for_each(|(num, base)| unsafe {
[841](#841)            *buf.get_unchecked_mut(base) = encode_pairs.get_unchecked(*num as usize)[1];
[843](#843)        });
[844](#844)
[845](#845)    10
[846](#846)}
[847](#847)
[848](#848)fn div_base_to_10(num: u128) -> (u128, u64) {
[849](#849)    let quotient = mulh(DIV_BASE_TO_10_MULTIPLY, num) >> DIV_BASE_TO_10_SHIFT;
[850](#850)    let remainder = num - BASE_TO_10 * quotient;
[851](#851)    (quotient, remainder as u64)
[852](#852)}
[853](#853)
[854](#854)const fn mulh(x: u128, y: u128) -> u128 {
[856](#856)    const LOWER_HALF_MASK: u128 = (1 << 64) - 1;
[857](#857)
[858](#858)    let x_low = x & LOWER_HALF_MASK;
[859](#859)    let y_low = y & LOWER_HALF_MASK;
[860](#860)    let t = x_low.wrapping_mul(y_low);
[861](#861)    let k = t >> 64;
[862](#862)
[863](#863)    let x_high = x >> 64;
[864](#864)    let t = x_high.wrapping_mul(y_low) + k;
[865](#865)    let k = t & LOWER_HALF_MASK;
[866](#866)    let w1 = t >> 64;
[867](#867)
[868](#868)    let y_high = y >> 64;
[869](#869)    let t = x_low.wrapping_mul(y_high) + k;
[870](#870)    let k = t >> 64;
[871](#871)
[872](#872)    x_high.wrapping_mul(y_high) + w1 + k
[873](#873)}
[874](#874)
[875](#875)unsafe fn _encode_buf(num: u128, digits: usize, buf: &mut [u8]) -> usize {
[876](#876)    unsafe { encode_impl(num, digits, buf, &STANDARD_TABLES.encode_pairs) }
[877](#877)}
[878](#878)
[879](#879)unsafe fn _encode_alternative_buf(num: u128, digits: usize, buf: &mut [u8]) -> usize {
[880](#880)    unsafe { encode_impl(num, digits, buf, &ALTERNATIVE_TABLES.encode_pairs) }
[881](#881)}

[888](#888)    #[must_use = "this allocates a new `String`"]
[901](#901)    pub fn encode<T: Into<u128>>(num: T) -> String {
[902](#902)        let num = num.into();
[903](#903)        let digits = digit_count(num);
[904](#904)
[905](#905)        unsafe {
[906](#906)            let mut buf = String::with_capacity(digits);
[907](#907)            let ptr = buf.as_mut_vec().as_mut_ptr();
[908](#908)            let slice = core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(ptr, digits);
[909](#909)
[910](#910)            let len = _encode_buf(num, digits, slice);
[911](#911)            debug_assert_eq!(len, digits);
[912](#912)
[913](#913)            buf.as_mut_vec().set_len(digits);
[914](#914)            buf
[915](#915)        }
[916](#916)    }
[917](#917)
[918](#918)    pub fn encode_buf<T: Into<u128>>(num: T, buf: &mut String) {
[932](#932)        let num = num.into();
[933](#933)        let digits = digit_count(num);
[934](#934)        let old_len = buf.len();
[935](#935)
[936](#936)        buf.reserve(digits);
[937](#937)
[938](#938)        unsafe {
[939](#939)            let vec = buf.as_mut_vec();
[940](#940)            let ptr = vec.as_mut_ptr().add(old_len);
[941](#941)            let slice = core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(ptr, digits);
[942](#942)
[943](#943)            let len = _encode_buf(num, digits, slice);
[944](#944)            debug_assert_eq!(len, digits);
[945](#945)
[946](#946)            vec.set_len(old_len + digits);
[947](#947)        }
[948](#948)    }
[949](#949)

[1146](#1146)    #[test]
[1148](#1148)    fn test_digit_count() {
[1149](#1149)        for pow in 1..22 {
[1151](#1151)            let this_power = (BASE as u128).pow(pow as u32);
[1152](#1152)            assert_eq!(digit_count(this_power - 1), pow);
[1153](#1153)            assert_eq!(digit_count(this_power), pow + 1);
[1154](#1154)        }
[1155](#1155)
[1156](#1156)        assert_eq!(digit_count(0), 1);
[1158](#1158)        assert_eq!(digit_count(1), 1);
[1159](#1159)        assert_eq!(digit_count(u64::MAX as u128), 11);
[1160](#1160)        assert_eq!(digit_count(u64::MAX as u128 + 1), 11);
[1161](#1161)        assert_eq!(digit_count(u128::MAX), 22);
[1162](#1162)    }

[1311](#1311)    fn test_decode() {
[1312](#1312)        assert_eq!(
[1314](#1314)            decode("00001000000000000000000000"),
[1315](#1315)            Ok((BASE as u128).pow(21))
[1316](#1316)        );
[1317](#1317)
[1318](#1318)        assert_eq!(decode("7n42DGM5Tflk9n8mt7Fhc7"), Ok(u128::MAX));
[1320](#1320)        assert_eq!(decode("LygHa16AHYG"), Ok(u64::MAX as u128 + 1));
[1321](#1321)        assert_eq!(decode("LygHa16AHYF"), Ok(u64::MAX as u128));
[1322](#1322)        assert_eq!(decode("0"), Ok(0));
[1323](#1323)
[1324](#1324)        #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
[1325](#1325)        {
[1326](#1326)            use alloc::string::String;
[1327](#1327)            let mut power = 1_u128;
[1329](#1329)            let mut power_minus_one_str = String::with_capacity(21);
[1330](#1330)            let mut power_str = String::with_capacity(22);
[1331](#1331)            power_str.push('1');
[1332](#1332)            for _ in 1..22 {
[1333](#1333)                power *= BASE as u128;
[1334](#1334)                power_minus_one_str.push('z');
[1335](#1335)                power_str.push('0');
[1336](#1336)
[1337](#1337)                assert_eq!(decode(&power_minus_one_str), Ok(power - 1));
[1338](#1338)                assert_eq!(decode(&power_str), Ok(power));
[1339](#1339)            }

# DecodeError in base62 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/base62/2.2.4/base62/enum.DecodeError.html

## Expand description

Indicates the cause of a decoding failure in base62 decoding operations.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ArithmeticOverflow)

### ArithmeticOverflow

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.EmptyInput)

### EmptyInput

The encoded input is an empty string.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidBase62Byte)

The encoded input contains the given invalid byte at the given index.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

Available on **non-crate feature **`std` only.

# decode in base62 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/base62/2.2.4/base62/fn.decode.html

`pub fn decode<T: `[AsRef](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.AsRef.html)<[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)]>>(input: T) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u128.html), [DecodeError](https://docs.rs/enum.DecodeError.html)>## Expand description

Decodes a base62 byte slice or an equivalent, like a `String`,
using the standard digit ordering (0 to 9, then A to Z, then a to z).

Returns a [ Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html) containing the decoded

[or a](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u128.html)

`u128`[.](https://docs.rs/enum.DecodeError.html)

`DecodeError`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
extern crate base62;
let value = base62::decode("rustlang").unwrap();
assert_eq!(value, 189876682536016);
```

---

# decode_alternative in base62 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/base62/2.2.4/base62/fn.decode_alternative.html

`pub fn decode_alternative<T: `[AsRef](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.AsRef.html)<[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)]>>(input: T) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u128.html), [DecodeError](https://docs.rs/enum.DecodeError.html)>## Expand description

Decodes a base62 byte slice or an equivalent, like a `String`,
using the alternative digit ordering (0 to 9, then a to z, then A to Z) with lowercase
letters before uppercase letters.

Returns a [ Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html) containing the decoded

[or a](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u128.html)

`u128`[.](https://docs.rs/enum.DecodeError.html)

`DecodeError`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
extern crate base62;
let value = base62::decode_alternative("rustlang").unwrap();
assert_eq!(value, 96813686712946);
```

# encode in base62 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/base62/2.2.4/base62/fn.encode.html

# Function encode

[Source](../src/base62/lib.rs.html#901-916) `pub fn encode<T: `[Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u128.html)>>(num: T) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

## Expand description

Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the standard digit ordering
(0 to 9, then A to Z, then a to z), and returns the resulting
`String`

[§](#example)Example

```
extern crate base62;
let b62 = base62::encode(1337_u32);
assert_eq!(b62, "LZ");
```

# encode_alternative in base62 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/base62/2.2.4/base62/fn.encode_alternative.html

Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the alternative digit ordering
(0 to 9, then a to z, then A to Z) with lowercase letters before uppercase letters,
and returns the resulting String.

---

# encode_alternative_buf in base62 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/base62/2.2.4/base62/fn.encode_alternative_buf.html

## Expand description

Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the alternative digit ordering
(0 to 9, then a to z, then A to Z) with lowercase letters before uppercase letters, and
then appends it onto the end of the given [ String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
extern crate base62;
let mut buf = String::from("1337 in base62 alternative: ");
base62::encode_alternative_buf(1337_u32, &mut buf);
assert_eq!(buf, "1337 in base62 alternative: lz");
```

---

# encode_alternative_bytes in base62 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/base62/2.2.4/base62/fn.encode_alternative_bytes.html

`pub fn encode_alternative_bytes<T: `[Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u128.html)>>(
    num: T,
    buf: &mut [[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)],
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html), [EncodeError](https://docs.rs/enum.EncodeError.html)>## Expand description

Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the alternative digit ordering (0 to 9, then a to z, then A to Z), and writes it to the passed buffer.

The return value is the number of bytes written to the buffer.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

- To encode all possible values of u128, the buffer must be at least 22 bytes long. However a smaller buffer may be used if the value to be encoded is known to be smaller. Base62 encoding adds 37.5% overhead to the size of the input.
- The remaining end of the buffer is left untouched. It’s up to the caller to zero it using the returned len if they want to.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
extern crate base62;
let mut buf = [0; 22];
base62::encode_bytes(1337_u32, &mut buf);
assert_eq!(&buf[..2], b"LZ");
```

---

# encode_buf in base62 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/base62/2.2.4/base62/fn.encode_buf.html

## Expand description

Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the standard digit ordering
(0 to 9, then A to Z, then a to z), and then appends it onto the end of the given
[ String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
extern crate base62;
let mut buf = String::from("1337 in base62: ");
base62::encode_buf(1337_u32, &mut buf);
assert_eq!(buf, "1337 in base62: LZ");
```

---

# encode_bytes in base62 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/base62/2.2.4/base62/fn.encode_bytes.html

## Expand description

Encodes an unsigned integer into base62, using the standard digit ordering (0 to 9, then A to Z, then a to z), and writes it to the passed buffer.

The return value is the number of bytes written to the buffer.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

- To encode all possible values of u128, the buffer must be at least 22 bytes long. However a smaller buffer may be used if the value to be encoded is known to be smaller. Base62 encoding adds 37.5% overhead to the size of the input.
- The remaining end of the buffer is left untouched. It’s up to the caller to zero it using the returned len if they want to.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
extern crate base62;
let mut buf = [0; 22];
base62::encode_bytes(1337_u32, &mut buf);
assert_eq!(&buf[..2], b"LZ");
```

---

# encode_fmt in base62 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/base62/2.2.4/base62/fn.encode_fmt.html

## Expand description

Writes the base62 representation of a number using the standard alphabet to any fmt::Write destination.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use core::fmt::Write;
let mut output = String::new();
write!(output, "{}", base62::encode_fmt(1337_u32));
assert_eq!(output, "LZ");
```

---

Source: https://docs.rs/base62/2.2.4/base62/fn.encode_fmt_alt.html

## Expand description

Writes the base62 representation of a number using the alternative alphabet to any fmt::Write destination.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use core::fmt::Write;
let mut output = String::new();
write!(output, "{}", base62::encode_fmt_alt(1337_u32));
assert_eq!(output, "lz");
```
